title: We are moving from searching for links to searching for answers.
body:
For years, the internet taught us to be good researchers. We would type a question into a search engine, scan a list of blue links, click one, and then mentally synthesize the information ourselves. It worked, but it was slow.

AI search is changing that habit. Now, we expect a direct answer immediately. We want the context, the nuance, and the summary without doing the heavy lifting of jumping between five different tabs.

But this shift creates a new problem. When you stop clicking through to original sources, you lose the ability to verify the information. You rely entirely on the AI to be accurate, which is a dangerous assumption in news.

At Headlinne, we believe the future of news isn't just about getting an answer. It is about getting the right answer from sources you can actually trust. We built our app to bridge that gap, giving you the speed of AI with the accountability of journalism.
cta: You can see how we are approaching this at HEADLINNE.com.
